text:
The Kraken's biggest move of the season happened off the ice. On Nov. 1 they traded Shane Wright, the fourth overall pick in 2022, to Nashville for Matthew Wood, and Wright promptly had a three-point night for the Predators. Wood picked up his first point with Seattle on Nov. 8. That trade will be judged for years; the team in front of it has a nearer problem.

Seattle is 9-8-1, and the record flatters it. The Kraken get only 43% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) and 44% at 5v5, and they've scored about nine goals more than those chances deserved. Our standings math says they've banked 3.6 more points than their play earned, and our playoff odds sit at 20%, with a projection near 82 points.

Two losses to Carolina in Finland made it three straight, outscored 13-5, with just 32% of the chances in those games. Philipp Grubauer has been 5.2 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, and Joey Daccord has been pulled twice in a week. Bobby McMann is running cold with two points in ten games.

The bright side is Berkly Catton: ten points in his last ten games and an eight-game point streak earlier this month, as KING5 reported. For Lane Lambert's team, what to watch is whether the returning Ryan Lindgren and Cale Fleury help tilt the ice, because Catton can't keep finishing for everyone.
